title: SLO-driven Pricing Storycards for Platform Sellers (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working set of short, repeatable storycards that platform sellers and solutions engineers can use when operational SLAs (latency/availability) are central to procurement conversations. The goal: turn technical SLOs into a pricing narrative that maps to risk, cost, and rollback policies — fast.

How to use this doc:
- Use the 30–60s lead for discovery calls.
- Pick persona-specific card(s) below and read the 2–3 bullet technical proof points aloud.
- When asked about cost, use the simple conversion (tokens -> ms -> $) in the Quick Numbers section.
- Run the POC checklist after the call if buyer asks for a viability test.
- Store feedback under #platform-sellers in Slack; tag PR/Confluence links in linked_artifacts.

30–60s Lead (script):
"Redwood lets product and infra teams guarantee user-facing LLM latency at scale while keeping unit cost predictable. We do this by routing requests to appropriate model variants, applying automatic prefix caching, and enforcing SLO-aware batching rules — so you can promise X ms P90 while controlling token spend. If the model variant is unavailable we automatically fallback to a cheaper compatible variant with no app changes.

Persona Cards (pick one)
1) Platform Architect (scale/ops worried about peaky load)
- Pain: unpredictable cost spikes during peak events + risk of SLO burns.
- Pitch: Dedicated pools + autoscale with burst caps = predictable throughput; SLO-driven routing routes latency-sensitive traffic to reserved capacity.
- Proof points: ability to reserve GPU slices per route; observed 40% reduction in P95 tail when KV-prefix caching is applied to conversational workloads in our internal benchmark (see linked PR).
- Hook: Offer a 2-week canary with a 10% reserved commit to measure tail latency under production traffic.

2) Product PM (wants quality guarantees and controlled costs)
- Pain: feature regressions when cheap quantized models are used; engineering overhead to swap models.
- Pitch: Redwood Optimize recommends model & quantization profiles based on real evals; rollouts are versioned so you can A/B and auto-fallback if quality regressions cross thresholds.
- Proof points: per-route eval hooks + automated rollback when eval score drops >3 points on owner-defined tests.
- Hook: Pre-populate 50–200 prompt-based evals during POC to baseline quality.

3) Procurement / Finance (needs pricing clarity)
- Pain: unpredictable usage bills and lack of guardrails.
- Pitch: Reserved capacity (Dedicated) for baseline spend + usage-based for burstable traffic; we provide per-token cost breakdown and token->ms conversion so you can model burn under expected QPS.
- Proof points: sample invoice template (see Confluence) and cost dashboard that breaks per-route/per-model unit economics.

Common objections + suggested responses
Objection: "We can just host an open model ourselves cheaper."
- Response: For SLOs you need operational investment (autoscaling, KV cache, routing, monitoring). Our internal estimate: N engineering FTEs x 6–9 months + variable infra ops. For many teams, that crosses the threshold where Dedicated capacity + Redwood support is cheaper and faster to production.
- Technical comeback: show the canary playbook (below) that demonstrates how we achieve 99th percentile latency improvements via kernel selection and batching.

Objection: "What if fallback hurts quality?"
- Response: We only fallback to verified compatible model variants and tie rollouts to evals. Default policy: fallback -> reduce max output tokens -> add system prompt to preserve format. If evals dip, auto-rollback and alert.

Objection: "How much will this cost at scale?"
- Response: Use Quick Numbers below to estimate. Show the buyer their expected QPS -> tokens per request -> per-token rate -> reserved capacity amortization. Offer to run a 48-hour traffic replay for a concrete estimate.

Quick Numbers (talking points you can say in call)
- Typical gen request (chat-like): 120–300 tokens in, 150–600 tokens out depending on prompt style.
- Conversion: on our hosted catalog, median token cost for a mid-sized open model = $0.0012 per 1k tokens (example only).
- Latency mapping: with SLO-aware GPU kernels and prefix cache enabled, median per-token decode is ~3–4ms on our benchmarked 80B quantized profile. So a 200-token response -> ~800ms decode plus attention/overhead -> ~1.1s median.
- Simple example: 100 QPS * 200 tokens/res = 20k tokens/s -> 1.44M tokens/day -> at $0.0012/1k => ~$1,728/day in generation cost (illustrative).

POC / Canary Checklist (10–15 minute summary to send as follow-up)
- Goals: measure P90 latency, per-token cost, and basic quality delta between baseline model and recommended variant.
- Inputs needed: 48–72h traffic sample or 1M sample prompts, SLO target (e.g., P95 <= 1200ms), billing contact, and access to customer test route.
- Steps:
  1) Create a dedicated route with SLO target and 10% traffic mirror.
  2) Enable prefix/KV cache + recommended batching config.
  3) Run traffic replay or mirrored production traffic for 48 hours.
  4) Collect per-route token counts, P50/P95/P99 latency, and eval set scores.
  5) Sync findings in a call and map to reserved commit options.
- Success criteria: P95 within target OR clear tradeoff mapping where reserved capacity reduces tail.

One-line technical proof snippets (for SEs to paste in chat)
- "We use SLO-aware routing to prioritize reserved capacity for latency critical routes and fall back to compatible variants if capacity is constrained — no SDK changes required."
- "Automatic prefix caching reduces repeated context compute and decreased P95 by ~30% on multi-turn dialogs in our internal tests."
- "Our runtime evaluates kernel selection per-request based on seq-length histograms so you don’t pay worst-case for typical short-turn dialogs."

FAQ (short)
- Q: Can customers bring their own model? A: Yes, Private supports BYOM with the same rollout and SLO tooling.
- Q: Do you support on-prem? A: Yes, Redwood Private + optional air-gapped deploys. Operational features (SLO routing) are available but require a light agent setup.
- Q: How fast can you start a 10% canary? A: Usually <48 hours once we have a route + auth and sample traffic.

Appendix: seller-side notes (things to not promise)
- Don’t guarantee exact ms numbers without a POC. Use ranges and be explicit about workload assumptions (seq lengths, parallelism, and top-k sampling settings).
- Avoid saying "free autoscale" for Dedicated — we offer burst/commit tiers with explicit terms.

Open questions / TODOs
- Get updated real-world per-token benchmarks for our top 3 catalog models (ask R&D for Feb 2025 benchmark CSV).
- Create a short 1-slide product explainer on SLO-aware routing for the next GTM all-hands. Owner: Ethan. Deadline: 2025-03-10.
- Draft two finance-friendly invoice examples for reserved vs hybrid pricing. Owner: Maya.

Source links & internal refs:
- Confluence: SLO Pricing Strategy (linked in header)
- Internal benchmark PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rg-ops/pull/614
- Slack: #platform-sellers (live feedback channel)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short. Sales decks should be the canonical slide pack; this is the quick conversational cheat-sheet.
- After 2 POCs, convert the highest-performing scenario into a reusable template in the sales playbook.
